newsitem.title: USA: Soy products end down, soyoil hits contract lows.
newsitem.headline: Soy products end down, soyoil hits contract lows.

text.p: Soy product futures ended lower Wednesday, and all soyoil months made fresh contract lows on heavy supplies, traders said.
"Supplies are huge and no one's buying," said one soyoil trader. "If you want to go short in a market, go short soyoil."
July soyoil fell to the lowest level for a nearby contract since November 15.

Weakness in cash soymeal markets in the U.S. and South American markets also pressured soymeal, traders said. Basis offers for soymeal in Illinois spot rail markets fell $1.00 per ton Wednesday on heavy supplies, cash traders said.
Basis in Brazil for soy pellets for August delivery has fallen $3.00 per ton in the last two days and supplies are building, said one trader with South American customers.
"The supply is there," said the trader. "Basis is falling for August, where everyone said they'd run out (of soymeal)."
Traders said that Iran was looking for 35,000 tonnes of South American soyoil for August delivery.
July soyoil ended 0.27 cent a lb lower at 22.46, and other months were 0.13 to 0.28 lower. July soymeal settled down $4.00 at $268.90, and other months were $1.00 to $3.70 lower.
In other export news, Egypt's state-owned holding company said it bought a total of 22,000 tonnes of palm stearin and palm oil for August delivery.
In soymeal trade, Cargill bought 300 lots July and 100 lots October and sold 300 lots August. Term Commodities sold 200 lots July and 100 December, pit traders said.
In soyoil trade on the day, Cargill bought 300 lots July, 400 August and 100 December. ADM bought 200 July and 200 August. Term Commodities bought 100 lots July and 200 August.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 22,925 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 34,000 lots, against Tuesday's 28,481.
